evidence: a-blacklisted-source-gets-nothing: lines 125-127 declare a DROP rule in INPUT for each ip_blacklist source and line 25 says those sources are 'dropped unconditionally'; pinging and opening SSH from the blacklisted +150 address and expecting both dropped tests that declaration under the fixture (ip_blacklist [peer+150]). The probe is derived correctly. The run's failure is a baseline finding, not an authoring error (see finding below).

policies-and-ssh-rules: lines 83-84 set the INPUT and FORWARD policies to drop, which the probe reads as -P INPUT DROP and -P FORWARD DROP. The second reference (135-137) plus the fixture (lab Hiera 127.0.0.1 + acl 192.168.56.1) give 2 '100 SSH whitelist' rules, and strict=false puts 116 in LIMIT_OVERALL. The expected values are the ones the code produces. OUTPUT ACCEPT is not managed by the class; the probe reads it but it matches the node and does no harm.

an-ssh-burst-is-cut-at-the-overall-limit: lines 132 and 153-154 give LIMIT_OVERALL 20/min with iptables' default burst of 5 and drop the rest (117). 20 parallel SYNs from an unlisted source after a 61 s refill let 5 in; a token refills every 3 s, which is longer than nc -w2, so a retransmitted SYN gets no token. Rules 112 and 114 can only drop more, never let more in, so 'in 5, dropped 15' is what the code produces.

finding a-blacklisted-source-gets-nothing: the peer saw 'icmp from blacklisted in / ssh from blacklisted in' where both should be dropped. I checked the applied node's iptables -S INPUT read-only: rule 666 (-s 192.168.56.174 -j DROP) comes after '000 ICMP limit' ACCEPT and after '110 SSH LIMIT_INDIVIDUAL' (whose chain ends in 116 ACCEPT). puppetlabs-firewall orders rules by title number, so the blacklist only drops what the earlier rules did not accept. The author's run 4 records the same failure.

finding the-rst-limit-dropped-the-third: rules 519 and 520 each counted 0 of the 3 in-connection RSTs, where 2 accepted and 1 dropped were expected. On the applied node, '003 accept related established rules' (state RELATED,ESTABLISHED ACCEPT) comes before 519 and 520, so those RSTs are accepted there. The set's own run-1 note says out-of-connection RSTs are dropped as INVALID by mangle rule 501, so 519/520 never see them either. The author's run 4 records the same failure.

purpose gap: Tested, all passing on the applied node: default-drop policies; SSH whitelist; the three SSH brute-force limits as real connection behaviour (burst 5, 8 held, 15 a minute); drops by mangle 501 and 502, read from their counters; the ICMP echo limit; only whitelisted sources reach the service through the side chain; the per-source connection limit and the new-connection rate on that chain; purging of unmanaged rules; the flush script plus rebuild on the next run. The two failing outcomes (blacklist, RST limit) are tested and are baseline findings. Gaps where the lab can exercise the behaviour: (1) Rule 503 (MSS outside 536-65535, line 166). The 'uncovered' reason (hping3 cannot set TCP options, the peer has no packet-crafting tool) is not true. The peer's python3, which this set already uses, can set TCP_MAXSEG before connect(); tcp(7) says this changes the MSS announced in the SYN, and the Linux minimum of 88 is below 536. 'ip route ... advmss' on the peer does the same. lifted_by names ubuntu2, the peer already in use, so nothing new would lift it. (2) Rule 518 (fragments, lines 184-185). The author measured it by hand on this lab (5 fragmented SYNs counted by neither 518 nor 501) and lists it as 'not a check yet', with lifted_by ubuntu, the default node. It is lab-exercisable and untested by a check, and the measurement points to a finding. (3) The outcomes table has no row for anti_ddos=true with ip_filter=false (lines 269-303: per-source connlimit and rate limits on INPUT for every source). The purpose names per-source limits, but only the side-chain variant has a row; it needs at least an honest uncovered row. (4) No row for rules 001 and 002 (lines 108-118: loopback accepted, 127.0.0.0/8 rejected unless it arrives on lo). Loopback acceptance can be exercised on the node. Uncovered rows I accept as honest: country_whitelist (xt_geoip and its database are installed by no class); internal_forward (needs a routed internal network behind the node; the class adds no SNAT); plain and strict modes (other fixture variants).
